evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month)).AddDays days
| true, Some days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))
| "net-eom" -> closed [ "days"; "kind" ] value |> Result.bind (fun () -> integer "days" value |> Result.map NetEndOfMonth)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule sits in Tier 1 or Tier 2. The due-date rule and the terms wording are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). Parsing and validating the form input is in Summa.Web.Engine (Tier 2), and the storage codec is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). Nothing in Tier 3 or Tier 4 is touched.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added. The changes are pure: the due-date calculation (DateTime.DaysInMonth is a pure calendar function, not a clock read), the text formatting, the JSON encoder and decoder built on the existing Json model, and the engine's pure input parser. No clock, I/O, randomness or console use is added.

evidence.quote: | false, Some days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(Net days))

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The words for the new terms are written twice: once in Documents.termsText and again in the private Invoicing.termsWords used by the audit trail. The two copies agree, but they can drift. This follows the existing Net/CustomDate pattern, which already duplicates. The 1..365 range guard is also copied into both match arms. The copies agree, so nothing contradicts.

evidence.quote: | DayOfNextMonth day -> let next = issueDate.AddMonths 1; DateOnly(next.Year, next.Month, day)
| false, true, Some day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording are in Summa.Ledger (Tier 1). Accepting form input is in the engine (Tier 2), and the codec is in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). No Tier 3 or Tier 4 code decides anything about the new terms.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effects are added. The due date is derived from the issue date passed in, not from the clock. The ordinal helper, the codec and the parser are all pure functions.

evidence.quote: if day >= 1 && day <= 28 then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day) else Error $"{day} is not a day of next month (1 to 28)"
| false, true, Some day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))
| DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The ordinal rule is defined once (Invoicing.ordinal) and reused, which is good. However, the 1..28 valid-day limit is written separately in the engine's form parser and in the storage decoder. Summa.Ledger, which owns the type and the dueDate that would throw for days above 28, does not define it. The phrase 'Due the … of next month' is also written in both Documents.termsText and Invoicing.termsWords. All the copies agree today, so this is restatement rather than contradiction.
